title: DAPD: Dependency-Aware Parallel Decoding via Attention for Diffusion LLMs
claim: Prior decoders unmask tokens in a sequential left-to-right pattern; ours unmasks many independent segments at once for global parallelism.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, token grids with green shading, numbered markers on ours
description: Two side-by-side panels show token grids of a diffusion LLM's partially decoded output after half of the decoding steps. Each token is a rounded box. Green boxes are already unmasked, and grey [M] boxes are still masked. Darker green marks the earliest unmasked tokens. Panel (a), DAPD (Ours), has unmasked text scattered across the whole sequence. Dark numbered markers [1] to [5] show five independent questions being answered at once, each with its own reasoning text such as the capital of North Korea and the Battle of Balaclava. Panel (b), Fast-dLLM, shows a solid green block at the start of the sequence, with only the first two or three questions filled in and a large masked region after it. The eye goes first to the scattered dark markers on the left and then to the contrast with the contiguous block on the right.
caption: Visualization of unmasking trajectories for DAPD (ours) and Fast-dLLM during the initial 50% of decoding steps. While DAPD processes independent questions simultaneously to maximize global parallelism, Fast-dLLM exhibits a highly sequential unmasking pattern. Other baselines demonstrate similar sequential behaviors (see [ref]). Detailed discussion is provided in Sec. [ref].
abstract: Parallel decoding for Diffusion LLMs (dLLMs) is difficult because each denoising step provides only token-wise marginal distributions, while unmasking multiple tokens simultaneously requires accounting for inter-token dependencies. We propose Dependency-Aware Parallel Decoding (DAPD), a simple, training-free decoding method that uses self-attention to induce a conditional dependency graph over masked tokens. At each iteration, edges in this graph capture strong token interactions, while non-edges indicate weak dependence. Parallel decoding is then reduced to selecting an independent set on the graph and unmasking the selected tokens in parallel. This avoids co-updating strongly coupled tokens without auxiliary models or retraining. Experiments on LLaDA and Dream show that DAPD improves the accuracy-steps trade-off over existing methods and enables more globally distributed parallel updates that better exploit the any-order generation capability of dLLMs. The project is available at https://ai-isl.github.io/dapd
